figure: locust circular-statistics composite (the reference page's panels with the letters following this figure's information flow: a setup, b model selection, c predictive check, d-f hypothesis testing)

panel_a_source.kind: extracted from the reference figure PDF
panel_a_source.note: image placements, vector paths and text spans read from the reference PDF and replayed; the sprite is the virtual-swarm photograph inside it

hypothesis_polar.note: observed-data band omitted; panel c draws it for each model

predictive_pair.estimate: von Mises KDE, histogram estimate omitted
predictive_pair.data_line: solid (dashed is the uniform reference on this page)

hypothesis_elpd_individual.reference: ELPD (log predictive density) per animal at each hypothesised direction; dots are animals, open markers the pooled values

corrections: panel a records 34 path primitives: the first extraction pass kept paths above y = 300 pt only and missed the two grey flight arrows of the bottom swarm's second row (y = 301-321 pt).

the panel letters and titles are not replayed from panel_a.json: the reference page's four letters and three titles are filtered out of the span replay and redrawn, because the flow (and so the wording of three of the titles) is ours.  Sizes and offsets are the reference's - 32 pt bold letters and 17 pt titles at 13.74 and 21.465 pt from the row top - but the titles are bold, matching the bat composite's panel titles.
panel d's arrows are drawn as a shaft plus a 16.8 pt triangular head in page points, i.e. panel a's arrow style; matplotlib's "-|>" head is blunter and shorter at the same nominal size.
panel d's polar tick labels are placed at their reference page positions: matplotlib puts polar tick labels on the grid circle, which lands "±180°" on top of the 180° grid line.
panel b prints four ELPD ticks where the reference page prints three, because our axis spans to -3581.7 rather than -3549.6.

panel d (the reference page's c) is not the reference page's panel any more: the observed-data band is gone (that comparison is panel c's, where each model's predictive density meets the data), the bimodal predictive density draws as a solid line over a tinted band, both over the dashed uniform circle, and the two hypothesis densities of panel e are marked at their directions - optic flow at 0 degrees, vectorial encoding at both +/-90 - against the uniform reference.  The markers are point estimates only: their +/-HDIs would be 3.6 pt long at the polar's scale (shorter than a marker), so panel e remains the place the intervals are read.

panel c is a pair of polar plots, one per model, each against the observed bootstrap KDE - the reference page had nothing there.  The observed KDE is drawn solid rather than the dashed line of the reference and the house panels: on this page dashed is the uniform reference (panel d's circle, panels e and f's vertical lines), and a dashed data line reads as a second uniform.  Each polar draws the model's line and band over the data: the data is the standard, the model is the subject.  Splitting the models is the point: on a shared axis the two bands lie so close together that the only reading is which is nearer the data.

panel c's polars are 68 pt radius against panel d's 118.7, so the two can share the page's left half with their horizontal tick labels; their labels sit at the reference page's own clearances (3.8-5.5 pt beyond the circle horizontally, 9.5-14 pt vertically) rather than its offsets scaled down, which would run the left "±180°" label off the page.

panel a's artwork shifts 40 pt right and panel d's polar 110.1 pt, each to sit visually centred with the panels below it: panel a's content centres on x = 249 pt, the content centre of b and of the c pair, and d's polar, like e's and f's axes, centres on x = 725.2 pt, the right column's axes centre - and so do the d, e and f titles.  The internal geometry of both panels (radii, ticks, weights, the artwork itself) is unchanged.

panel f's axes height is read from the house swarm's own y limits after it draws (4 * the stack reach + 4 * the packing clearance = 202.5 pt at dot 4.5 pt and gap 1.25) and the axes re-placed to it: the swarm sets its limits in points, so the axes height has to equal that number or the packing the function computes is not the packing that gets drawn - and the height is not predictable from the dot size alone, because the greedy packer's stack reach is not monotonic in the packing distance.  Dots are packed 1.25 times their own diameter apart: packed at their own size they only touch, and the vectorial-encoding row, where all 52 animals fall within 1.2 ELPD, then reads as one solid block.
known_differences: The page is 900 x 900 pt against the reference's 900 x 600: panels c and f are new in a third row of 300 pt, and the letters follow this figure's flow of information (setup, model selection, predictive check, then hypothesis testing at three levels), so the reference page's c and d are d and e here.  Their internal geometry is kept exactly as measured, as is b's; what differs is where content sits inside a column - panel a's artwork and panel d's polar shift right to centre on the panels below them, and the d, e and f titles centre over the same x.
Text is set in Arial; the reference page uses Helvetica Neue, whose glyph widths differ by 1-4% at the same size and position.
Panel b's cached unimodal fit gives ELPD -3533.40 +/- 38.34 where the reference page prints -3502.0 +/- 38.8; the bimodal fit matches (-3404.51 +/- 39.27 against -3403.8 +/- 39.2).

stable_panels_against_the_previous_build.method: text spans and drawing primitives of row 2 (panels b and e, the panels the reference page has that were neither repositioned nor restyled), compared between the previously committed PDF and this one; the panel letters and titles are excluded, they are redrawn to this figure's flow
stable_panels_against_the_previous_build.png_note: the page is 900 x 900 pt in both builds, so unlike the previous change of page height this one keeps the raster phase of the whole figure; the shifts (panel a, panel d, the titles) are the only things that move.

mean_abs_pixel_difference_against_refere.regions: panel a: x 72-492, y 5-350; panel b: 28-448, 360-520; panel d: 595-900, 5-350; panel e: 455-880, 360-520 (pt, top-left origin); panel a's and panel d's crops compare the artwork at its shifted position (the reference crop is taken 40 pt / 110.1 pt to the left), so the numbers measure the drawing, not the centring move.  d's number is above the previous build's 12.9 because the model density now draws as a solid saturated line and band over the uniform circle, where the reference page draws it faint.
mean_abs_pixel_difference_against_refere.method: 300 dpi, with the best shift within +/-4 px taken up.  Panels c and f are new and have no reference panel.
